guard.strictOutcomeForRequestedPlacement: Guard would ABORT: assert(geometry.classification === "fully-offscreen") fails with "Test window intersects an active display; stop and restore approved offscreen placement" because classification is "partially-visible".
guard.partialOutcomeForRequestedPlacement: With --allow-partial-visibility the visibility assert passes (classification "partially-visible" != "fully-visible"); remaining preconditions: windowState "normal", width>=800, height>=600 (1200x900 passes), frontmostPid != browserPid.
guard.guardRunnableReason: browser-focus-guard.mjs is a macOS-only observer: it probes /usr/bin/osascript (NSScreen + NSWorkspace) and /usr/sbin/lsof, neither of which exists here (test -x rc=1 for both; lsof exists only at /usr/bin/lsof). No Linux display probe exists in the pinned guard.
guard.noGuardObservationStatement: No guard observation exists here. Nothing in this record was produced by running the guard or any substitute for its probes. classification "partially-visible" is arithmetic on host display geometry using the guard’s own pure-function logic, and the real window bounds under Wayland must be read back from the browser before any guard result is claimed.

waylandPositionCaveat: Chromium under Wayland cannot set absolute window positions: there is no global client-visible coordinate space, so left=2400/top=120 is a request only and the GNOME/Mutter compositor decides the final placement. The real bounds must be read back from the browser (CDP Browser.getWindowForTarget/Browser.getWindowBounds) and this arithmetic re-done on the observed values before any classification is trusted.
